_about: Seed catalog of public sources for procedural landscapes. 'license' is what we expect; the harvester records what it actually finds in 'license_found' (catalog/harvest_report.json). Only permissive licenses may have code adapted; copyleft is study-only. Datasets carry their own terms.

repos.why: Fully procedural natural worlds in Blender: tree, plant, rock, terrain, creature and material generators. Closest prior art for the whole project.
Parametric three.js tree generator with presets; good reference for browser-side LOD and leaf billboards.
Earlier three.js procedural tree work by the same author.
Compact classic procedural tree generator (snapshot-style trees).
repos.note: No LICENSE file in repo: all rights reserved by default. Study only.

repos.why: Constraint-based tile synthesis; useful for town layouts, fences, field patterns.
Industry-standard navmesh + crowd steering; target for scaling fauna beyond grid A*.
Large-terrain clipmap LOD and texturing; reference for streaming tiles at multiple resolutions.
Particle hydrology with streams, pools and vegetation feedback — the next step beyond our thermal erosion + D8.
repos.note: No LICENSE file at repo root: treat as all rights reserved; study the technique (and the author's blog posts) only.

repos.why: Minimal particle-based hydraulic erosion.
repos.note: No LICENSE file at repo root: study only.

repos.why: Clear droplet erosion implementation.
Fast portable noise library (OpenSimplex2, cellular, domain warp) with Python/JS ports.
Reference OpenSimplex2 implementations; public domain.
Instanced grass field with wind in three.js — reference for blade-level grass in the viewer.
repos.note: Non-commercial licence (some individual files MIT). Do not copy; study the instanced-grass technique only.

repos.why: Agent-based modelling framework; patterns for schedulers, data collection and batch runs.
Learned animal behaviours later (RL policies on top of the utility layer).
Plate/precipitation/biome world generation — macro context for tiles.
Settlement, road and river placement heuristics at map scale.
Viewer runtime (pinned r128 to match PORTOS).
Water shading reference for creeks, ponds and Gulf shoreline.
US building footprints for real-place mode.
Sapling Tree Gen (Weber & Penn) lives here — study the parameterisation, don't copy code.
repos.note: No root LICENSE file; Blender add-ons are GPL by convention (per-file headers). Study only.

repos.why: OSM-to-Blender buildings/terrain import; study only.
repos.note: No root LICENSE file found by the probe; GPL per project docs. Study only.

repos.why: Compact PBR reference for bark/leaf/soil materials.

datasets.name: USGS 3D Elevation Program (3DEP)
datasets.use: Lidar-derived DEMs (~1 m in much of the South) as the real terrain base.

datasets.name: USDA NAIP aerial imagery
datasets.use: ~0.6–1 m orthoimagery for land cover, canopy and texture guidance.

datasets.name: National Land Cover Database (NLCD)
datasets.use: 30 m land cover and tree canopy to seed biomes.

datasets.name: USFS Forest Inventory and Analysis (FIA)
datasets.use: Real species mix, density and size distributions by county.

datasets.name: Silvics of North America (Ag. Handbook 654)
datasets.use: Species heights, diameters, habitat — verify species.py against it.

datasets.name: USDA PLANTS Database
datasets.use: Native ranges and plant characteristics for grasses, shrubs, trees.

datasets.name: OpenStreetMap
datasets.use: Roads, buildings, paths, water for real-place mode.

datasets.name: Poly Haven
datasets.use: Bark, soil and ground textures/HDRIs for the viewer.

datasets.name: ambientCG
datasets.use: PBR materials (bark, gravel, metal roof, siding).

datasets.name: Movebank animal tracking
datasets.use: Real deer/turkey movement statistics to calibrate fauna — check each study's terms.
